notes.safety: All four display guarded/compacted relationships and shorter exposed tails/support posture. Defense style varies with the inherited source form; no new stock shell is used.
notes.security: The 0% column spreads the occupied core/roots into a wider brace in all four examples. The effect is clearest in the relative separation of source masses.
notes.trust: The 0% and100% columns differ in anterior exposure, head/body overlap and tail/effector reach. This is clearer under matched comparison than as a universally readable emotion; small/crowded cranial forms remain a limitation.
notes.rest: Low Rest reduces fullness and crouches/supports the existing source form; high Rest visibly restores fullness. Seed2 low Rest remains a weaker native64 comparison than the other three.
notes.relaxation: The 0% column visibly holds a different regional bend/tension arrangement;100% matches neutral as intended. Static images cannot establish natural motion.
notes.physical-fitness: Low/high Fitness change existing load-bearing fullness and recruitment posture, without adding supports. Seed2 low Fitness is less conspicuous at native64; positive Fitness is clearer.

limitations: A bounded debug subset of existing proof conditions; no population or full care-gate percentage.
